text: If we relocate a skid and move its Tessera gateway to another site in TesseraCloud, does the old vibration history move with it?
evidence: Historical readings remain associated with the original site and assets. They are not moved.
Their asset and measurement point bindings are cleared and must be re-created in the destination site.
answer: No. Historical readings stay with the original site and assets; the paired nodes move with the gateway but their asset and measurement point bindings are cleared and must be re-created.

text: Can Meridian's support engineers just log into our TesseraCloud tenant and look at our data when we open a case?
evidence: Meridian Support engineers cannot see tenant data by default.
Access is read-only unless "Allow configuration changes" is also selected, and it expires automatically after 7 days.
answer: No. A Tenant Owner has to grant time-boxed access (Settings > Security > Support Access, quoting the MSC ticket number); it is read-only by default and expires after 7 days.

text: Why would a Lumen flow meter read zero when there is definitely water going through the pipe?
evidence: The meter declares an empty pipe when the optical path sees no fluid for longer than the detection delay.
Confirm the pipe is full. Check that the meter is not at a high point and that vertical installations have upward flow
answer: It has declared an empty pipe (L-201): the pipe is running partly full, air is collecting at a high point, or the detection delay is too short. Check the installation and lengthen the empty-pipe detection delay (default 5 s; 30 s recommended for gravity or pump-cycled lines, max 120 s).

text: Is there a hardware way to lock an LF-60P so nobody can change its settings, not even remotely over HART or Modbus?
evidence: when S3 is ON, no parameter can be changed from the display, HART or Modbus.
Holding registers are write-protected when DIP switch S3 on the terminal board is ON; writes then return exception code 04.
answer: Yes. Set DIP switch S3 on the terminal board to ON; no parameter can then be changed from the display, HART or Modbus (Modbus writes return exception 04).

text: Nobody on site remembers the supervisor code for one of our HX-210s. Can we reset it from the detector itself?
evidence: It cannot be reset from the instrument itself.
it can be reset from Meridian Link (Instruments > Security > Reset Passcode) by a user with the Fleet Administrator role.
answer: No. It can only be reset in Meridian Link (Instruments > Security > Reset Passcode) by a user with the Fleet Administrator role.

text: Does TesseraCloud charge us for every vibration sensor we stick on a machine?
evidence: TesseraCloud subscriptions are billed per monitored asset per year, not per node.
Asset subscriptions are counted per asset, not per node.
Subscriptions are an annual operating cost billed per asset, not per node.
answer: No. Subscriptions (TC-SUB-STD / TC-SUB-ENT) are billed per monitored asset per year, not per node; an asset with several nodes counts as one.

text: What paperwork has to be in the box when a customer sends a gas detector back for repair, so it doesn't just get sent back unopened?
evidence: Every return must include a completed and signed Decontamination Declaration, form MI-F-031
Units that arrive without form MI-F-031 are quarantined unopened and returned to the customer at the customer's cost.
answer: A completed and signed Decontamination Declaration, form MI-F-031 (uploaded to the RMA and in a clear pouch on the outside of the carton). Without it the unit is quarantined unopened and returned at the customer's cost.

text: We just commissioned Tessera at a new plant and it has fired dozens of vibration alarms in the first week. Are the nodes faulty?
evidence: TesseraCloud learns an operating baseline over the first 14 days of data for each asset.
alarm thresholds left at the generic defaults rather than set for the machine class
After 14 days of data, TesseraCloud computes a baseline for each measurement point
answer: Usually not. Baselines are still being learned for the first 14 days (adaptive alarms suppressed, only absolute ISO 10816 zone alarms active), and thresholds may be at generic defaults or the wrong machine class, or nodes may be mounted on non-rigid covers.

text: Can I send a worker into an area where hydrogen might be present with only an HX-200 on them?
evidence: It must not be used in Zone 0 or in gas group IIC atmospheres such as hydrogen or acetylene.
Do not propose it where hydrogen or acetylene may be present. Those gases fall in group IIC.
answer: No. The HX-200 (II 2G Ex ib IIB T4 Gb) is approved for gas groups IIA and IIB only; hydrogen is a group IIC gas.

text: During a pump overhaul, how long can we mute Tessera alarms on that asset before they come back on by themselves?
evidence: Maintenance mode has a maximum duration of 72 hours per activation.
When it expires, alarm evaluation resumes automatically
answer: Up to 72 hours per maintenance-mode activation; alarm evaluation then resumes automatically and a new activation is needed if work continues.

text: The engineer who built our TesseraCloud integration has left the company. Will the API keys they created keep working?
evidence: API keys bound to a named user stop working when that user is deactivated
Keys bound to an Integrator account are unaffected by staff changes.
answer: Not if they were bound to that person: keys bound to a named user stop working when the user is deactivated. Keys bound to an Integrator service account are unaffected.

text: What's the recommended way to pull a couple of years of vibration history into our data warehouse without getting throttled by the API?
evidence: For historical backfills and data-warehouse loads, use export jobs (POST /v2/exports) instead of paging through the readings endpoint.
Bulk historical data should be extracted using export jobs rather than repeated calls to the readings endpoint.
answer: Use asynchronous export jobs (POST /v2/exports), each covering up to 31 days of raw readings or 12 months of hourly aggregates, instead of paging through the readings endpoint.

text: Does bump testing an HX-210 adjust the sensors the way a calibration does?
evidence: a brief exposure to a known gas to confirm that sensors respond and alarms operate. It does not adjust the instrument.
adjustment of the zero and span of each sensor using a certified gas mixture.
answer: No. A bump test only confirms that the sensors respond and the alarms work; calibration adjusts each sensor's zero and span.

text: Why is the HX-220 only good for Zone 1 when the HX-210 is allowed in Zone 0?
evidence: The lower protection level (ib rather than the ia of the HX-210) is a consequence of the larger 5,200 mAh battery and the radio module.
answer: Because its larger 5,200 mAh battery and radio module limit it to Ex ib protection (Zone 1 and 2) instead of the HX-210's Ex ia.

text: An HX-210 has been sitting in a store cupboard for about five months. Can we just charge it up and hand it out?
evidence: must be calibrated before use, because the calibration countdown continues during storage.
answer: No. After more than 120 days in storage it shows CAL DUE and must be calibrated before use, because the calibration countdown continues during storage.

text: What does E-117 mean on a Halcyon detector and what's the fix?
evidence: LEL sensor poisoned or catalytic bridge fault
Do not attempt recalibration. Replace the LEL sensor HX-SNS-LEL-04 following section 4 of sup-hx-sensor-replacement-procedure, then perform a full calibration.
answer: LEL sensor poisoned or catalytic bridge fault (HX-210/HX-220). Do not recalibrate; replace the HX-SNS-LEL-04 sensor per section 4 of the sensor replacement procedure, then do a full calibration.

text: Our integration is getting HTTP 429 with TC-ERR-429 from TesseraCloud. What does it mean and what should the client do?
evidence: Rate limit exceeded; honour Retry-After
Clients must honour Retry-After and use exponential back-off with jitter.
answer: The API rate limit was exceeded. Honour the Retry-After header and retry with exponential back-off and jitter; a key that keeps getting 429s for 15 minutes is suspended for 10 minutes.

text: What is Tessera event T-348?
evidence: Store-and-forward buffer above 90% after a long backhaul outage
When the buffer reaches 90% the gateway raises event T-348 (buffer near capacity)
answer: Buffer near capacity: the gateway's store-and-forward buffer is above 90% after a long backhaul outage. Restore backhaul; once full, the oldest readings are overwritten.

text: Which Modbus input register do I poll to get the active L-code from a Lumen meter?
evidence: When more than one error is active, register 30018 returns the lowest-numbered code.
over Modbus (input register 30018)
answer: Input register 30018 (numeric part of the L-code; lowest-numbered code if several are active, 0 if none).

text: What is part number HX-FLT-D4?
evidence: Dock inlet filter (annual replacement)
Replace the inlet filter HX-FLT-D4 every 12 months.
answer: The inlet filter for the HX-DOCK-4 docking station, replaced every 12 months.

evidence: Select Device > Firmware Update and choose the image LF60P_1.9.0.mfw.
answer: LF60P_1.9.0.mfw (the meter must already be on 1.8.2, using Meridian Link 4.2 or later).

text: Which Modbus holding register sets the HART poll address on an LF-60P, and what is it by default?
evidence: HART poll address
The default is 0, which keeps the loop current active.
answer: Holding register 40020 (LF-60P only); default poll address 0.

text: What does TS4-GLD-KIT-02 replace and what's different about it?
evidence: the gland kit TS4-GLD-KIT-02 replaces the older TS4-GLD-KIT-01; the new kit adds an EMC gland for M20 entry 1

text: An HX-210 is throwing E-117. Once the new sensor is in, how tight do the bracket screws go and how long before I can calibrate it?

Refit the retaining bracket and tighten the two Torx T6 screws to 0.25 N m.
Leave the instrument switched on in clean air for a warm-up period of 4 hours before calibrating.
answer: Replace HX-SNS-LEL-04 per section 4: tighten the two Torx T6 bracket screws to 0.25 N m, then leave it on in clean air for 4 hours before calibrating.

text: Our HX-210s keep failing span with E-104 since the firmware update. What's the usual cause, and what gas and flow should we be using?
evidence: For the HX-210 follow section 5 of prod-hx210-calibration-procedure-v2
Using MI-CAL-Q4-A with firmware 3.4.1 is the most common cause of E-104 on the LEL channel.
Flow: confirm the regulator is MI-REG-10 (1.0 L/min).
answer: Most often the discontinued MI-CAL-Q4-A mix is still being used with firmware 3.4.1. Use MI-CAL-Q4-B at 1.0 L/min through an MI-REG-10 regulator (section 5 of calibration procedure v2).

text: A gateway is flashing red and reporting T-327. What do we have to enter on the gateway to fix it, and how long do we have to do it?
evidence: Re-provision the certificate with a one-time provisioning token

Go to System > Cloud > Provisioning Token, enter the token and select Apply.
answer: Re-provision the expired certificate: generate a one-time 12-character token (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) in TesseraCloud (Security > Re-provision Certificate) and enter it in the gateway local UI at System > Cloud > Provisioning Token. The token is valid for 24 hours and can be used once.

answer: Gateway firmware 5.3.0; node 2.8.0 is only supported on 5.3.0. Update the gateway first, then the nodes.
